milestone.title: Consumer-surface de-internalization — strip milestone IDs, lesson codes, and dead doc refs from skills + docs; add a leak guard

intent.outcome: External adopters never see this repo's plan history on any shipped surface: skills (templates/skills/**), docs (docs/** except docs-old/), and adopter-facing READMEs carry no internal milestone IDs (M\d+), no lesson codes (L\d), and no pointers to repo-internal files. Every skill and doc directive keeps its exact meaning; only provenance tokens and dead links change. A ripgrep guard in `make lint` keeps the surface clean going forward.

problem.description: The deployed skills and shipped docs leak this repo's internal vocabulary onto the consumer surface. An mp-runner execution flow lists 'M147 consult FIRST', 'M113 advisory lock', and 'L5' — provenance an external agent cannot resolve (it has no `mp show milestone M147` in its repo). Inventory: ~90 milestone-ID refs (M76-M173) and ~30 lesson-code/dead-link refs across 13 templates/skills files plus docs/. Worse, `docs/code-review-lessons.md` is referenced 13x but has been archived to docs-old/ (a dead link for consumers AND stale in-repo), and `docs/dogfood/M110-s5-audit.md` is referenced by mp-code-review but does not exist. Not a blocker today, but it causes documentation rot and gaps over time and undercuts the self-contained-toolkit mission. Complementary (not blocking): milestone 194 covers the mp-init-GENERATED AGENTS.md doc refs; this milestone covers the deployed skills + docs + READMEs surface.

in_scope: templates/skills/**: strip internal milestone IDs (M\d+) and lesson codes (L\d) from the consumer skill bundles (mp-runner, mp-coordinator, mp-flow, spec-grill, codebase-design, diagnosing-bugs); preserve every directive's meaning.
docs/** (excluding docs-old/): strip milestone IDs, lesson codes, and dead repo-internal file pointers.
Adopter-facing READMEs (root README, install/quickstart): same de-internalization pass.

Core skills (mp-runner/mp-coordinator/mp-flow): delete the dead docs/code-review-lessons.md and docs/dogfood/M110-s5-audit.md pointers and strip the L-code labels — the L1-L7 pre-screen prose is already inlined in reviewing.md/executing.md, so no redirect is needed (and core must not depend on an opt-in skill).

mp-code-review is master-plan-repo-only (Q-03 decision): remove it from the consumer catalog so `mp install` does not deploy it, and document it as repo-internal in docs/skills/README.md (NOT in the category table). As a repo-internal skill, the consumer-surface de-internalization rules do not apply; fix only its dead docs/code-review-lessons.md pointer.
Vendored skills (codebase-design, diagnosing-bugs): drop the internal M146: provenance prefix; keep the upstream mattpocock/skills MIT attribution.

Add a ripgrep leak guard (\bM\d{2,4}\b, \bL\d{1,3}\b, and the dead-link paths) over templates/skills/ + docs/, with a synthetic-ID allowlist (e.g. the mp path pin 42 --before 17 CLI example), wired into make lint.

crates/ source: judgment-call pass — remove gratuitous provenance refs, RETAIN genuinely-useful design-rationale pointers (audience = repo maintainers with plan access). Lower priority than the consumer surface.
out_of_scope: master-plan/** — the plan zone; milestone IDs are the native vocabulary and stay.
mp-dogfood-log.md and repo-internal dogfood notes — internal, not consumer.
Restoring or re-shipping docs/code-review-lessons.md as a consumer doc — the review checklist is canonically inlined in the mp-coordinator reviewing sub-mode; the doc stays archived.
Making core skills depend on mp-code-review (or any opt-in catalog skill) — core must stay self-contained or reference only other core skills.
Stripping M-codes/L-codes from mp-code-review — it is master-plan-repo-only, not a consumer surface.
Hard-banning milestone IDs in crates/ source — soft pass only (keep where genuinely needed).

design_decisions.choice: Hard-ban internal provenance on the consumer surface (skills/docs/READMEs); soft-pass crates/ source.
design_decisions.rationale: crates/ is read by repo maintainers who have plan access, so a milestone-ID pointer to design rationale can be legitimate there; the consumer surface has no such audience. Reconciles crates/ appearing both in- and out-of-scope during grilling.

design_decisions.choice: Core skills (mp-runner/mp-coordinator/mp-flow) stay self-contained: the L1-L7 pre-screen is already inlined in reviewing.md/executing.md — strip the L-code labels and the dead docs/code-review-lessons.md pointer; core never redirects to an external skill. mp-code-review (catalog/opt-in) is cleaned as a self-contained power-up, NOT a dependency.
design_decisions.rationale: mp-code-review is category catalog (opt-in) while the core three deploy by default — pointing core at an opt-in skill would break for adopters who did not install it. The L1-L7 prose is already inlined in the core skills, so the dead pointer is deleted, not redirected. This finishes the migration M99 intended (subsume the review checklist into the mp-coordinator reviewing sub-mode); mp-code-review stays optional runnable-fixture automation.

design_decisions.choice: Manual review sign-off is the completion gate, not the guard.
design_decisions.rationale: The top risk is behavior drift — rewriting prose to strip tokens can subtly change agent behavior; a regex guard cannot detect semantic change, so a review comparing intent before/after is the real acceptance signal. The guard is prevention, not the gate.

design_decisions.choice: The AGENTS.md 'Consumer-surface hygiene' convention and the docs/skills/README.md 'Authoring rules' section (landed this session) are the foundation; this milestone is the cleanup + guard.
design_decisions.rationale: The rule + docs prevent new leaks; this milestone clears the existing ~120 refs and adds enforcement.

design_decisions.choice: Minimal edits: remove the provenance token, keep the directive; per-file review compares intent before/after.
design_decisions.rationale: Stripping tokens must not alter what an agent does at execute/review time. Flagged as the top risk during grilling; the guard cannot catch it.

design_decisions.choice: Allowlist entries are CLI-example synthetic IDs only (e.g. `mp path pin 42 --before 17`), documented inline at the guard.
design_decisions.rationale: Unconstrained synthetic-ID exemptions could backdoor real leaks.

design_decisions.choice: Core skills (default-deployed: mp-flow, mp-runner, mp-coordinator) must not depend on catalog/opt-in skills (spec-grill, mp-code-review, codebase-design, diagnosing-bugs).
design_decisions.rationale: A default mp install deploys only the three core skills; an opt-in skill is absent unless explicitly requested. A core skill that points at an opt-in skill sends a default adopter to a missing target. Opt-in skills are additive power-ups; core stays self-contained or references only other core skills.

open_questions.question: mp-code-review self-containment may surface deeper dependencies — it refs crates/mp/tests/code_review_patterns.rs. Does that path ship in the deployed bundle, or must the pattern list be inlined into the skill before other skills repoint to it?
open_questions.answer: Resolved by the cleaner-resolution redesign: core skills will NOT repoint to mp-code-review (it is opt-in catalog; core must stay self-contained). The dead pointers are deleted, not redirected; the L1-L7 prose is already inlined. mp-code-review is cleaned as a standalone opt-in skill.

open_questions.question: mp-code-review is category catalog (opt-in) and is currently missing from the docs/skills/README.md category table. Should this milestone add it to the table (documenting it as an opt-in runnable-fixture runner), or is documenting it out of scope here?
open_questions.answer: Resolved: yes — document mp-code-review in the docs/skills/README.md category table as a catalog (opt-in) entry. This milestone already rewrites that file and clarifies mp-code-review role (D2/D7). Folded into the amended mp-code-review in_scope bullet.

open_questions.question: mp-code-review portability: its runnable patterns live in crates/mp/tests/code_review_patterns.rs (master-plan-repo-only). To make the skill self-contained for consumers, either (a) vendor the pattern list/run-commands into the skill, or (b) document mp-code-review as master-plan-repo-only and remove it from the consumer catalog. Decide before approval.
open_questions.answer: Resolved per recommendation: mp-code-review is master-plan-repo-only. Its runnable patterns are coupled to this repo test fixtures (crates/mp/tests/code_review_patterns.rs) and the archived lessons doc, so it is not portable to consumer projects. Decision: remove mp-code-review from the consumer catalog so mp install does not deploy it, and document it as repo-internal in docs/skills/README.md rather than vendoring fixtures into the skill. Consequence: mp-code-review is no longer a consumer-surface de-internalization target; in_scope bullet 5 amended to repo-only treatment (only its dead docs/code-review-lessons.md pointer gets fixed).

findings.description: mp-code-review SKILL.md references crates/mp/tests/code_review_patterns.rs and tells the agent to run cargo nextest -p mp --test code_review_patterns — a master-plan-repo-internal path absent from every consumer project. in_scope bullet 5 only enumerated docs/code-review-lessons.md and docs/dogfood as dead pointers; this crates/ ref is a third dead internal pointer and is not trivially deletable since it IS the skill core mechanism. Surfaced during challenge CH-195-01.

consumer-surface lint allowlist was line-anchored only; adding a line above an allowlisted location silently breaks the exception. Fixed: allowlist entries now require a 'label:file:line:anchor:reason' 5th field (anchor substring), and is_allowlisted matches line+anchor. Verified with shifted-line and anchor-changed tests. (scripts/check-consumer-surface.sh)

consumer-surface lint had no self-test; patterns could fall into disrepair without the main lint noticing. Fixed: added --self-test mode that creates a known-violation fixture in a temp dir, runs the guard against it, and asserts each pattern catches >=1 violation. Self-test output: 'caught 7 violation(s) across the fixture (milestone-id:3,lesson-code:2,dead-code-review-lessons:1,dead-dogfood:1)'. (scripts/check-consumer-surface.sh)

consumer-surface lint used 'mapfile -t' (bash 4+) which fails on macOS bash 3.2. Fixed: rewrote the rg-excludes construction to a while-read loop on a process substitution. Verified on macOS bash 3.2. (scripts/check-consumer-surface.sh)

consumer-surface lint used 'mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t ...' but the -t form is deprecated on BSD mktemp. Fixed: introduced mktemp_dir() and mktemp_file() helpers that try BSD/GNU-compatible templates first. (scripts/check-consumer-surface.sh)

mp-coordinator SKILL.md Stage-8 auto_remediate section replaced 'see crates/mp/src/config.rs' with 'the install source for the parser' — vague. Fixed: dropped the path reference entirely and described the parser's contract inline. (templates/skills/mp-coordinator/SKILL.md)

AGENTS.md 'make consumer-surface-lint' description ended with '(M195)' — a leaked milestone ID, exactly the kind of provenance the lint forbids. Fixed: description rewritten to 'flags internal milestone IDs, lesson codes, and dead doc pointers'. (AGENTS.md)

Q-03 incomplete: mp-code-review remains category=catalog and is still installable via `mp install --skills=mp-code-review` (templates/skills/mp-code-review/manifest.json; SKILL.md Install section; crates/mp/tests/install_skills_v2.rs still asserts deploy succeeds). Scope required removing it from the consumer catalog so adopters cannot receive a skill coupled to crates/mp/tests/code_review_patterns.rs and docs-old/. Docs mark it repository-internal, but the install path still ships it. Fix: make the skill non-selectable (e.g. category=internal + reject in validate_selection, or drop from SkillRegistry), remove the Install section, and update install_skills_v2 accordingly.
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: Behavior drift in core skills: after deleting the docs/code-review-lessons.md pointer, reviewing.md/SKILL.md/planning.md/mp-runner still tell agents to 'read the lesson-pattern library directly' and call it the 'canonical source' / 'source of truth' (e.g. templates/skills/mp-coordinator/reviewing.md:5, :46, :91-94, :177) while D2 said the L1-L7 pre-screen is inlined and the dead pointer is deleted, not redirected. reviewing.md also asserts 'patterns are not duplicated' then lists key patterns. Agents will search for a missing doc. Fix: make the inlined pre-screen the sole source; drop external-library language.
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: Allowlist F-02 incomplete in scripts/check-consumer-surface.sh: is_allowlisted still requires exact line_e == line AND anchor (lines 223-226), contradicting the header comment that line is a hint and anchor is authoritative. A one-line insert above an allowlisted site still breaks the exception (false-positive lint). Self-test covers pattern catch only, not allowlist shift/anchor. Fix: match on file+anchor (treat line as optional diagnostic), and extend --self-test to assert a shifted-line still allowlists when anchor matches.
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: Guard scope gap: script header and milestone in_scope claim coverage of adopter-facing READMEs (root README, install/quickstart), but SCAN_PATHS only includes templates/skills and docs (scripts/check-consumer-surface.sh:41-44). Latent hole if a leak lands in README.md. Fix: add README.md (and any other adopter-facing entrypoints) to SCAN_PATHS, or narrow the documented scope to match the code.
findings.author: external-review

findings.description: dead-dogfood allowlist entry anchors on 'paths `docs/code-review-lessons.md`' rather than a docs/dogfood substring (ALLOWLIST line for docs/skills/README.md:191). It works only because both dead paths share one line; splitting the sentence would leave the dogfood match unallowlisted or over-allow unrelated lines. Fix: anchor on 'docs/dogfood' for the dead-dogfood label.
